# Attained logarithmic buffer-scale selection and its extended nonregular separator

This completes Sections 1--2 of
`candidate b4f092ee1bb5a205` in the
established compact minimal-bad-base framework. The scalar/body/parameter
minimum is actually attained. At that minimum the already audited
finite-contact physical response construction extends to both signs of
dot(log epsilon), and its SAME separator satisfies Delta=tau M.

Attainment is proved below from the compactness framework. The separator
statement retains the precise actual-cover, addable-speed-cone and uniform
shape-envelope premises of the existing nonregular response theorem; no
new assertion that an arbitrary formal tangent cone is physical is made.
No optimized-value derivative or Gamma payment is used or proved.

## 1. Standing framework and value gap

Fix a canonical cardinality-minimal hypothetical bad base P, its inherited
affine lattice, continuous dimension d>=1, N=d+1, and occupied parity count
k. Let beta_* be the infimum of ordinary normalized maximum depth over ALL
positive compatible families on P. Assume the already established framework:

1. beta_*<b<Gamma_d/k; every original sublevel beta_0<=b has representatives
   with M=1, uniform positive fiber volumes/inradii, bounded fibers and
   positive covariance, and the required closed-minor quotas at limits.
2. The transformations making those representatives are common continuous
   affine changes and affine base shears, under which the invariant buffer,
   the concave parameter class and its logarithmic normalization are invariant.
3. Parameters initially belong to the enlarged nonnegative upper-semicontinuous
   concave class, positive on sampled fiber interiors, with mean log L=0.
   Canonical sampled hypograph roofs are used for compactness.
4. The audited compactness/positivity package is that in
   `candidate f17e4f2b0ba9ee84`
   and `candidate c3d41384eb67bd52`.

The independently audited quantitative face theorem
`candidate 5dc06bb8226350eb`
gives constants 0<c<=C and epsilon_bar>0 such that

    beta_*+c epsilon <= b(epsilon) <= beta_*+C epsilon,
    b(epsilon)=inf_(K,L) beta_epsilon(K,L),
                                      0<epsilon<=epsilon_bar. (1)

Decrease epsilon_bar so epsilon_bar<1 and all these assertions hold. Its
choice is fixed before tau is varied. An arbitrary fixed P with a bad
number is not being assumed to supply this framework automatically.

## 2. Actual attained scalar/body/parameter minimum

For tau>0 minimize over actual bodies, parameters, and 0<epsilon<=epsilon_bar

    J_tau(K,L,epsilon)=beta_epsilon(K,L)-tau log epsilon. (2)

For tau small enough the legal trial epsilon=tau/C gives, using an attained
slice minimum or arbitrarily close slice competitors,

    inf J_tau <= beta_*+tau[1+log C-log tau].           (3)

This tends to beta_* and is therefore below b. Take a minimizing sequence
whose objective is below b. Since epsilon<1, its nonnegative penalty implies
beta_epsilon<=J_tau<b, and hence beta_0<b. The bodies admit the common compact
positive representatives in Section 1.

The scalar coordinate cannot approach zero at fixed tau, since

    J_tau>=beta_*-tau log epsilon ->infinity.

Thus its minimizing sequence lies in some [a_tau,epsilon_bar] with a_tau>0.
The fixed-epsilon logarithmic parameter compactness proof is UNIFORM on this
scalar interval. Explicitly, if sampled maxima diverged, their normalized
concave array and the limit minor quotas would give a base of limiting base
depth at least 1/k with diverging centroidal multiplier. The physical buffer
there diverges because epsilon>=a_tau. It would force beta_epsilon>=1/k-o(1),
contradicting b<Gamma_d/k<1/k. The normalization then bounds every sampled
maximum away from zero, and the same boundary-layer estimate gives uniform
integrability of log L.

After a subsequence, epsilon has a positive limit; the bodies and canonical
concave parameters converge in the audited interior/logarithmic topology.
Their actual buffers converge uniformly, since the scalar epsilon also
converges and energy vanishes on fiber boundaries. The all-normal slab
comparison gives convergence of beta_epsilon, including pure-base caps.
The logarithmic normalization and admissibility survive. Hence (2) is
attained in the enlarged class.

Every attained triple minimizes the UNPENALIZED body/parameter problem at
its own fixed epsilon: otherwise that slice could be improved without
changing the penalty. The existing sampled-majorant and actual boundary-cut
arguments therefore apply without modification. They give an equivalent
attained triple with

    L=min_(1<=i<=q) A_i>0 on its compact canonical hull,
    q<=|P|,

and a positive extension to a neighborhood. No positivity was assumed for
the compact limit before those arguments were applied.

## 3. Interior scale selection with explicit constants

Let epsilon_tau be the scalar coordinate of any attained triple. Comparing
(1) with (3), and writing s=epsilon_tau/tau, gives

    c s-log s<=1+log C.                               (4)

In particular

    a tau<=epsilon_tau<=b_0 tau,
    a=1/(e C),  b_0=(2/c)log(2C/c).                   (5)

For the lower estimate discard c s>0 in (4). For the upper one use the
global tangent bound

    log s<=(c/2)s+log(2/c)-1.

Since C>=c, b_0 is positive. For all sufficiently small tau, b_0 tau is
strictly below epsilon_bar. Thus epsilon_tau is an INTERIOR scalar
minimizer, and both signs of its infinitesimal logarithmic variation are
actually feasible. No differentiability of b(epsilon), envelope theorem,
or body convergence rate has entered this proof.

As tau tends to zero, these are exact unpenalized joint minimizers on their
chosen slices, with epsilon_tau tending to zero. Therefore the previously
proved physical-buffer vanishing, uniform source interiority and uniform
proper-own-trace conclusions apply. Their constants are independent of tau.

## 4. The actual additional direction in the finite-contact continuation

Retain the full hypotheses and notation of
`candidate 1a7cfa3d1047cbae`.
In particular there is an actual finite old covering by proper groups and
compressed atomic rows, with finite contact sets, strict off-cover gaps,
uniform signed shape envelopes, and an addable physical/parameter test cone.
Inside supporting hinges are conservatively omitted with full body capture
retained; outside hinges and their consistent selectors are kept.

For any allowed actual path and any real scalar s, add

    epsilon(t)=epsilon exp(s t).

This is a legal simultaneous path, since the old epsilon is interior.
Its body and parameter parts are unchanged. Products with existing first
variations contribute only higher-order terms; the new first buffer change
at contact a is exactly s delta_ia, where delta_ia=epsilon f_ia.

Consequently the old exact contact budget becomes

    alpha_ia'=old_alpha_ia' -s delta_ia,
    alpha_i'=min_a alpha_ia'.                          (6)

The sign follows directly from the contact expression
sum rho N.w-h_0-epsilon f(w)sum rho Gamma(u): an increasing epsilon lowers
its minimum. Free normal controls remain shared across contacts exactly as
before. No supporting-facet selector is freely reassigned.

Each conservative equalized loss ell_i is still jointly concave in the
old actual directions, normal controls, and s, because its scalar budget
has merely acquired the displayed linear term. The minimum over contacts
remains exact for that conservative response. For an atomic row the raw
loss is independent of s; its fixed pure-base cap remains a covering cap
for every nearby epsilon.

If D is the total first volume loss, the derivative of a group's normalized
upper bound for (2) is at most

    (beta D-ell_i)/M -tau s.

Thus its conservative IMPROVEMENT is

    ell_i-beta D+M tau s.                              (7)

If all row improvements were positive, the same actual continuation and
strict-gap argument would give a strict descent of (2). This is impossible
at the attained triple. The old concave hypograph separation therefore
applies to the product of the actual cone with the full scalar line R.
Finite actual speed addition is unchanged; epsilon jets add because
exp(s_1 t)exp(s_2 t)=exp((s_1+s_2)t).

For an entire tested physical/parameter class, the same compact-selector
finite-intersection argument supplies ONE dual for that class AND both
signs of s. Appending this one-dimensional variable introduces no new
selector compactness or closure assumption. It does not justify enlarging
the old physical cone by unrealizable body jets.

## 5. Exact scalar stationarity in the SAME separator

Use the old common contact/branch weights lambda_iab and atomic weights,
whose total is one. A contact's budget is multiplied in its linear
equalized loss by 1/B_ib. Therefore the scalar contribution of (6) is

    -s sum_iab lambda_iab delta_ia/B_ib=-s Delta,
    Delta=sum_ia kappa_ia delta_ia,
    kappa_ia=sum_b lambda_iab/B_ib.                   (8)

The penalty term in (7) is common to every row, including atomic rows, so
its averaged coefficient is M tau s. Both signs of the actual scalar
variation in this SAME separator force

    Delta=M tau.                                      (9)

An atomic-only separator is now excluded even by (9), since its Delta
would be zero. The earlier actual atomic-hinge exclusion remains valid.

Testing body and parameter directions with s=0 gives exactly the previous
physical density, logarithmic volume martingale, gradient labels and flux
identities. There is NO extra body or parameter penalty term, because
-tau log epsilon is constant along those separate variations. In particular
the beta occurring in the body density is the original normalized buffered
depth beta_epsilon, not the penalized numerical value J_tau.

If M_*<=M<=M^*, (5) and (9) give

    M_*/b_0 <=Delta/epsilon<=M^*/a.                   (10)

These are actual same-force bounds, not derivatives of an optimized value.
The previously proved Delta<=epsilon S_max is consistent and still holds.
Sections 3--4 of the root source may now use (10), provided their actual
row likelihood and uniform source-core hypotheses are retained.

## 6. Exact ordinary interval calibration

The following is an actual safe example, not a hypothetical bad one. Take
n=0,d=1,K=[-1,1], L=1. Then M=E(0)=2, Sigma=1/3. For 0<epsilon<sqrt(3),

    beta_epsilon=1/2+epsilon/(2sqrt(3)),

uniquely at zero. Indeed at x the two buffered directional fractions have
minimum

    1/2-|x|/2+epsilon sqrt(1-x^2)/(2sqrt(3)),

capped by one; this is strictly smaller away from zero. For ANY positive
concave log-normalized L, concavity of log L gives L(0)>=1, so the value at
zero is at least the displayed optimum. Every one-dimensional convex body
is affinely equivalent to this interval, with the same invariant buffer.
Thus this really is the global ordinary interval-class parameter optimum.

The scalar minimizer of (2), when inside the selected epsilon interval, is

    epsilon_tau=2sqrt(3)tau,
    beta_epsilon_tau=1/2+tau.

The actual two-cap group has coarea 1/sqrt(3), hence

    K=1/sqrt(3),  Delta=epsilon_tau/sqrt(3)=2tau=M tau.

This checks the normalization and sign in (9) independently of the bad-body
framework. It gives no new mixed Gamma bound.

## 7. Scope

Sections 1--3 prove genuine penalized attainment and an interior scale in
the stated compact minimal-bad framework. Sections 4--5 prove that the
audited nonregular actual response package extends to that scalar direction
with no new regularity assumption and no optimized-value derivative. They
retain the package's exact finite-cover and physical-cone premises.
The resulting Delta=M tau is a concrete normalization of the SAME force.
It does not by itself complete a cap-payment argument or identify the
original-volume and tilted-row means.

The companion `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_log_buffer_scale_separator_defect_transport.py`
checks the exact scalar coefficients and the actual interval calibration.
